Develop new ETL jobs to integrate product or business data into our warehouse
Improve the performance and reliability of core pipelines
Build reusable datasets that support experimentation, product and business analytics, or cross-functional stakeholders
Document and simplify complex data workflows for broader use

Experience coding in Python or a similar language and writing SQL queries
Experience building or working with data pipelines, ETL, or large datasets
Curiosity about how data systems work and interest in making them more scalable and reliable

The Rendering & Animation team (R&A) builds the graphics engine which renders the canvas for all Figma applications. Our mission is to make rendering performant, feature-rich, reliable, maintainable and extendible across all products & surfaces. The team plays a core, bedrock role for the company because it underpins the technology driving the user experience, touching many other teams, and as such is one of the most impactful areas of Figma.
The R&A team is devoted to hiring individuals with graphics expertise. We are interested in a variety of sub-domains, including 2D GPU-driven rendering, computational geometry & vector graphics, animation frameworks, anti-aliasing algorithms, shader effects, and more recently branching into video/image processing. A PhD Intern specializing in any of these areas would be a phenomenal fit for the team with a lot of exciting projects available.
As an intern on our team, you'll take ownership of a high-impact project at the intersection of your technical strengths and our most pressing graphics, rendering, or media challenges. You'll work closely with your intern manager, team leads, and collaborators across 1–2 partner teams to deliver tangible results within your internship. This is an opportunity to do significant, portfolio-worthy work that directly supplies Figma's visual platform.
This is a 12 or 16-week internship role that can be held from one of our US hubs (San Francisco or New York) starting in May or June of 2027.
What you'll do at Figma:
Learn from industry graphics engineers and participate as an embedded team member of the Rendering & Animation team
Collaborate with engineers, PMs, designers, and researchers to scope and execute your work
Develop, validate, and document solutions from prototypes to production-ready systems
Drive projects that apply research insights to meaningful product challenges
Contribute to exciting domain areas; some examples: crafting and optimizing shaders for sophisticated effects, investigating improvements to anti-aliasing algorithms, improving media processing capabilities, animating spline interpolation, and more!

Current enrollment as a 4th or 5th year senior PhD student pursuing a PhD in Computer Graphics, Media Processing, or a related field
Experience working with OpenGL, WebGL, WebGPU, Vulkan or Metal and their respective shader languages (GLSL, WGSL) or other low-level graphics APIs
Proficiency in either C++ or Rust
A track record of rigorous problem-solving through academic or applied research, with experience thinking holistically about use cases and the low-level technology required

Demonstrated expertise in computer graphics, supported by publications at conferences such as SIGGRAPH, Eurographics, High Performance Graphics, NVIDIA GTC, or Pacific Graphics
Proficiency in WebAssembly, web graphics, 2D graphics, performance optimization, animation, geometry, or media
Interest in art and design applications

title: Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community you will join:
The Chief Business Officer (CBO) organization drives Airbnb's growth and expansion around the world, commercializing our new and existing businesses and executing our global strategy in the market. The Global Markets team sits within CBO and makes sure Airbnb is locally relevant everywhere we operate, working with regions to plan and execute growth across supply, demand, and the surfaces our communities use.
Asia is one of the largest growth opportunities in that portfolio and one of the most complex regions to run: Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia sit at very different stages of maturity, with distinct competitive sets, regulatory contexts and consumer behaviour. Over the past year, the region has built a new operating system and scaled multiple growth levers from single-market pilots to regional programs. That growth has outpaced our capacity to run it: business reporting, program delivery and the cross-functional roadmap currently sit with one person alongside the regional strategy agenda. We are building a dedicated capability to own how Asia operates and how Asia delivers, and we want you at the centre of it.
The difference you will make:
This role is based in Singapore and requires regular travel across Asia.
In this role you report to the Senior Business Operations and Growth Lead, Asia and work closely with country Business Operations and Growth Leads across Japan, Korea, India and Southeast Asia, alongside central teams in growth marketing, product, payments, supply, policy and brand. You own the Asia business reporting and operating cadence, and you lead the delivery of the region's growth levers and its cross-functional roadmap.
This is deliberately an ownership role in insights and execution, distinct from the roles around it. Countries own their market plans and outcomes, growth marketing, product and merchandising teams build the platforms, and Strategic Finance and Advanced Analytics own objective tracking and measurement standards. You own the connective tissue between them: the reporting that gives the region one accurate and current picture, the delivery of growth levers into market, the roadmap accountability that keeps cross-functional commitments on track, and the competitive read that tells us where we are gaining and losing.
A typical day:
Lead the end-to-end operations and delivery of selected regional growth levers including go-to-market, measurement and optimization
Own the regional business reporting structure, inputs and cadence regionally and globally
Own the regional view of the cross-functional roadmap across supply, product, payments, policy, brand and growth marketing, and drive accountability on delivery through cross-functional collaboration
Own the regional competitive view across both guest and host and enable capabilities locally for country teams for local competitors
Build AI-enabled automation into the region's reporting, insight delivery and recurring operations that scales team output
Synthesize data, trends, guest and host insights, and analysis into actionable recommendations for the regional business
Conduct deep dives into operational, programs or functional topics as needed, working with FP&A to assess business performance across areas of strength and weakness
Drive entity prioritization and lead entity setup across Asia markets, coordinating with legal, tax, finance and country teams
Your expertise:
10+ years in business operations, strategy, consulting or program management, ideally in a marketplace, consumer technology, hospitality or online travel agency (OTA) environment
Experience managing programs or operations across multiple countries with varying levels of maturity, and across time zones
A proven track record building and running business operating cadences for a distributed organization: reporting, business reviews, and the follow-through that makes commitments land
Exceptional cross-functional orchestration in a heavily matrixed organization, creating clarity where ownership is split across product, growth marketing, payments, supply and country teams
Strong operating discipline: cross-workstream roadmaps, launch management, business reviews and executive reporting, and crisp written communication that keeps distributed teams aligned
Builds operational leverage with AI: a track record of applying AI and automation to reporting, insight generation and repetitive operational work, with measurable time saved or scale gained. You treat this as part of how you work, not a side project.
Analytical fluency: comfortable in the numbers, builds the analysis personally, and sets consistent measurement standards with analytics and finance partners (Excel)
Thrives in ambiguity, with a strong bias to action, ownership and ruthless prioritization
Fluent written and spoken English
Desirable: hands-on experience with one or more growth levers such as incentives, promotions and coupons, host-funded offers, lifecycle and CRM, or merchandising. Familiarity with the business, economic and cultural environments across Asia.

title: Product Manager, Social Features
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join: 
Our Product Marketing Managers start with the guest and work backwards, turning product thinking, data, and research into strategy. They own outcomes end to end, lead cross-functional teams across engineering, design, data science, and program management, and stay close enough to the details to know when something is off.
The Social team is making Airbnb a place where you travel with, and because of, the people you know. Our strategy has three parts: scaling the social graph, building social features that make Airbnb fun and useful for you and your friends, and creating social experiences that help people form new relationships and strengthen existing ones in real life. Each part has its own dedicated pod of engineers, designers, and program partners.
The Difference You Will Make
As Product Marketing Manager for Social Features, you'll lead a new pod that turns guests' connections into reasons to come back to Airbnb. You'll own the features people use with their friends: the travel map and sharing it, group travel tools, recommendations from people you know, and how connections are woven across Airbnb to make the whole travel experience better. You'll own the outcome, not just the roadmap: you'll make the calls on scope and priority with a dedicated engineering lead, engineers, and design partner, and be accountable for the results. You'll take features from brief to launch, use experiment results to decide what to build next, and grow how often guests plan, book, and share trips with the people they know. You'll also write the product narrative that explains each release to leadership and to guests.
A Typical Day
Work backwards from the guest: write crisp briefs and requirements for new features, each grounded in a real guest need and a clear definition of success
Prototype with AI first: build working prototypes yourself to explore ideas, test them with guests, and align the team in days rather than weeks
Drive execution with engineering, design, data science, and program management, from concept through launch and iteration, often with several features in flight at once
Go deep with the team on the details: review builds, test flows yourself, and chase down the edge cases that decide whether a feature delivers for guests
Shape how connections are integrated across the guest journey, from search and booking to Trips, so planning and traveling with people you know feels natural
Build shareable, delightful moments like the travel map that bring new people to Airbnb and grow the social graph

You will own the business operations agenda for the UKI and Nordics. Airbnb’s most established European market alongside five high-potential Nordic markets (Sweden, Denmark, Norway, Finland). Turn complex data into clear narratives that help leadership decide with a recommendation attached.

title: Senior Growth Marketing Lead (SEO, AEO, GEO)
description:

The Community You Will Join
Organic search is one of Airbnb's largest and most efficient acquisition channels, and the rise of AI answer engines is reshaping how travelers discover places to stay, things to do, and trusted Hosts. This role sits at the intersection of growth marketing, content strategy, and emerging AI search behavior, partnering closely with product, engineering, content, and data science teams to make Airbnb the trusted source that search engines and AI models cite.
The Difference You Will Make
As Senior Growth Marketing Lead, SEO, AEO, GEO, you will own the strategy and day-to-day execution for how Airbnb shows up in Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and the assistants that come next. You are an execution-focused operator with a career built in SEO — you write your own SQL, size opportunities from raw data, and ship. Success in this role means measurable gains in organic visibility, rankings, AI citations, traffic, bookings, and downstream conversion, along with a measurement framework that proves the business value of organic channels. This is a chance to define what AEO and GEO mean for Airbnb and build the playbook others follow.

Own the organic growth strategy and content roadmap across SEO, AEO (Answer Engine Optimization), and GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) — covering technical SEO, content, on-site experience, and visibility in AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Gemini, and Perplexity.
Manage internal content strategy for these acquisition channels: set priorities, briefs, templates, and quality standards for content and landing pages that drive organic and AI-referred traffic.
Run the channel hands-on — pull and analyze your own data in SQL, size opportunities, prioritize by impact, and drive launches and experiments from backlog to measured result.
Lead cross-functional relationships with product and engineering teams, embedding SEO and AEO best practices into web properties, app surfaces, and structured data.
Improve how well AI models understand Airbnb's listings, product, and policies so they represent Airbnb accurately and cite it as a source.
Build and evolve the measurement framework for SEO, AEO, and GEO — attribution models, leading and lagging indicators, dashboards, and revenue impact — including the ability to demonstrate the value of work that's difficult to attribute, such as preventive technical work or emerging AI channels.
Establish Airbnb's point of view on how AI-generated answers are reshaping travel discovery, and translate complex technical concepts into clear business narratives for senior leaders.

10+ years of experience in SEO, including 2+ years in a senior/leadership capacity engaging with executives.
Strong SQL skills, writing your own queries to analyze crawl, log, search console, and conversion data without relying on analysts for core questions.

Expertise in both technical SEO and content strategy, including site architecture, structured data, indexation, and content quality.
Working knowledge of how AI-powered search and answer engines operate (LLM-based retrieval, citation behavior, entity recognition), with a clear point of view on how to optimize for them.
Strong analytical foundation, comfortable with attribution challenges and building measurement frameworks that quantify the business impact of organic channels.
Experience working cross-functionally with engineering, product, content, and data science teams to implement SEO and AEO improvements at scale, and a track record of developing and retaining high-performing teams.
Preferred: experience in a two-sided marketplace or travel business where listing, location, and user-generated content pages are major organic surfaces; background in international SEO across multiple markets and languages; experience building programmatic or product-led SEO at scale; early-mover experience in AEO/GEO visibility monitoring and optimization; hands-on skill with Python, BigQuery, or similar tools and log/crawl analysis at scale.

description:

Airbnb's Business Technology (Biztech) organization sits at the heart of how we scale our internal operations to match the pace and ambition of our products. Within Biztech, the Finance Accounting Platform team owns the core finance accounting platform — the system that records, processes, and reports the financial lifecycle of every product Airbnb offers to the world. This is a senior finance systems product role: you are the product owner for the platform, its roadmap, and its controls.
As a Senior Platform Manager on this team, you will be embedded in a rich, cross-functional community spanning the full breadth of Airbnb's business. You'll partner daily with Product and Platform Managers across Payments, Trust, Guest & Host, Pricing, Insurance, Hotels, and Customer Service — as well as Finance stakeholders from Revenue Controllership, Treasury, Tax, Payments Legal, Consolidation, Collections, and Cash. You'll work closely with Data Engineers and Oracle Applications teams to bring platform solutions to life, and collaborate with FP&A and Business Unit teams who depend on the data your platform produces.
This is a role for someone who thrives at the intersection of finance, product, and engineering — often someone who started in accounting or audit and moved into finance systems or a techno-functional product management role — and who finds energy in being the connective tissue across a large, diverse, and highly capable community. Additionally, you bring in that broad perspective and proven track record of implementing platform solutions that scale to changing business needs
The Difference You Will Make:
You will be the strategic and operational owner of the finance accounting platform — the single point of accountability for shaping how it evolves to support Airbnb's growing portfolio of product offerings. Your impact will be felt across three dimensions:
Scaling the platform with Airbnb's ambitions — You will define and drive the long-term roadmap for the finance accounting platform, ensuring it can scale to support new product lines, geographies, and business models. You will own prioritization across a high-volume platform funnel — balancing competing requests with clarity and structured decision-making — and continuously identify opportunities to optimize platform performance and reliability.
Bringing new products to life on the accounting platform — Every time Airbnb launches or evolves a product, there is an accounting story that needs to be told accurately and at scale. You will lead that effort end-to-end — from initial accounting impact assessment through solution design, engineering alignment, UAT, release coordination, and production normalization — translating complex product changes into well-designed accounting workflows that record product lifecycle financials to Oracle FAH GL.
Strengthening the financial foundation — You will help define and refine data pipeline monitoring and SOX controls, support month-end close processes, and partner with Finance stakeholders to automate manual operational workflows. Your work will directly improve the accuracy, timeliness, and reliability of financial data that flows across Airbnb's Finance organization and beyond.
A Typical Day: 
No two days look the same, but here’s a window into what you might be doing:
Syncing with a cross-functional Product Manager from the Payments or Hotels team to understand an upcoming product change and assess its downstream accounting implications
Reviewing a product spec with Data Engineering to align on the implementation approach for a new accounting workflow feeding Oracle FAH
Running a UAT session with Revenue Controllership and Tax stakeholders to validate that a new product's financial lifecycle is being recorded accurately before it goes to production
Pulling and analyzing ad hoc data using SQL to support a Finance or FP&A team working through a close question or business case
Triaging and prioritizing new requests coming into the platform funnel — aligning stakeholders on sequencing and tradeoffs against the broader roadmap
Reviewing data pipeline monitoring alerts and working with engineering to resolve a control gap before it impacts month-end close
Leading a working session with Treasury or Collections to map out an opportunity to automate a high-touch manual process
Prototyping an AI-assisted workflow to automate a recurring reconciliation, journal, or intake-triage task, and defining the validation and human-review controls around it
Drafting a platform update for a senior Finance stakeholder that translates a complex technical change into clear business impact

Accounting & Finance Domain
CPA, CMA, or equivalent accounting credential strongly preferred; Big 4 audit or controllership background a plus
Subject matter expert in accounting principles and ASC 606 revenue recognition, with the ability to apply standards to complex, multi-product digital marketplace environments
Proven experience implementing end-to-end accounting workflows across record-to-report and order-to-cash cycles, including SOX controls, reporting, and reconciliation
Hands-on experience supporting high-volume, event-driven transactional workflows (bookings, payments, payouts, refunds, adjustments) on finance platforms in a marketplace or payments environment — ideally at a high-growth technology company
Platform & Product Management
6+ years (typically 10+) of experience in platform management, product management, finance systems with a strong business, finance and accounting data focus
Demonstrated ability to own and manage a complex, multi-stakeholder platform roadmap with a high volume of competing priorities
Proven track record of driving end-to-end delivery — from design and engineering through testing, release, and production normalization — in cross-functional environments
Experience operating in Agile and continuous delivery models; able to move with pace without sacrificing rigor or quality
Technical Depth
Actively uses AI tools to accelerate your own work and to automate repetitive finance workflows (journals, reconciliations, close tasks, intake triage), with a clear view of the validation and control implications before release
Experience working with or alongside Oracle FAH, General Ledger, or equivalent ERP platforms
Solid SQL skills and proven ability to work with large, complex datasets — including writing performant queries against partitioned tables, aggregating high-cardinality transactional data, and troubleshooting data anomalies at scale
Familiarity with subledger to General Ledger data flows — understanding how product-level financial events are transformed, aggregated, and posted as journal entries, and how to validate accuracy across that chain
Working fluency in modern data pipeline concepts (batch vs. streaming, partitioning, warehouse vs. lake) sufficient to engage Data Engineering on design tradeoffs; you don't need to build pipelines, but you need to reason about them
Familiarity with data pipeline architecture and monitoring controls — including SLA management, data quality checks, alerting frameworks, and reconciliation workflows that ensure financial data integrity across the close cycle
Communication & Collaboration
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to modulate depth and style based on audience — from engineering spec reviews to
Finance leadership briefings
Strong influencing skills and high EQ; proven ability to drive alignment across diverse, senior stakeholders without direct authority
Detail-oriented and highly analytical; comfortable structuring ambiguous problems and driving to clear outcomes
Proficiency with Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, and modern collaboration tools
Education
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Accounting, Finance, or a related technical field

title: Senior Platform Product Manager, Trust and Safety
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join: 
Our hosts are opening their homes or providing experiences to guests from around the world. We’re creating new relationships & placing people in vulnerable situations. Therefore trust is the fundamental currency of Airbnb. We are the Trust & Safety team, composed of engineers, data scientists, designers, product managers, and operations, responsible for earning this trust by building for safety at each moment of the guest and host journey. We build cutting edge machine learning models to detect risk, defenses to deter risky actors, and operations tools that enable investigators worldwide. We define community standards and policies, set high expectations, and keep bad actors out while providing delightful experiences for good users.
The Difference You Will Make:
As a Product Manager in the Trust & Safety team, you will identify customer pain points, business opportunities, and define/deliver the products that help us create a safe and trusted community around the world. Your work will be pivotal to shaping the future of hospitality and travel. Within the Trust & Safety team, you’ll be focused on Safety: To reduce safety incidents (e.g. interpersonal harm and illegal activities).

Creating vision and strategy for Trust & Safety products and platforms. 
Leading a cross-functional working group of engineers, data scientists, designers, operations experts, and policy experts to ensure alignment, execution, and launches
Maintaining product backlog and the product roadmap. Own prioritization process of product solutions based on business value and customer impact
Defining goals and success with clearly measurable objectives and key results. 
Building alignment across product teams (inside and outside of Trust & Safety), and Leadership/Executive teams.
Anticipating bottlenecks, making tradeoffs and balancing the business needs, customer needs, versus technical or operational constraints.
Presenting product roadmap and status to the business and Airbnb leadership on an ongoing basis. Communicate concisely and influence outcomes.
Evaluating new product opportunities and bring forward proposals (buy, build, partner solutions) for new capabilities with data and users at the forefront 
Developing short term plans aligned with long term goals to iteratively build platform capabilities to defend against safety issues
Becoming the thought leader and entrepreneur that others within Airbnb look up to for knowledge, processes, and methods on building products and platforms
Your Expertise:
5+ years product management experience
Prior product, operation, or engineering experience in trust, safety, risk or fraud 
Outstanding written and verbal communication ability to a diverse stakeholder audience, including a global team of C-level executives, product, and technical stakeholders
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills
Experience building machine learning products or technical product management

Entrepreneurial drive to achieve stretch goals in an innovative fast-paced environment

title: AI Solutions Program Manager, Finance
description:
Who we are  
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
You'll be joining the Finance Operational Excellence team, reporting to the Head of Finance Operational Excellence. We are finance transformation and AI experts working side-by-side with Finance, Product, and Engineering teams to redefine processes and build the finance organization of the future. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys working across disciplines: part solution developer, part data architect, part workflow designer, and part coach. You’ll have room to shape how applied AI is built and scaled both from a technical and end-user perspective.
What you’ll do
You'll work side-by-side with Finance subject matter experts to understand how work gets done, identify the highest impact opportunities, and partner with domain teams to chart a transformation plan which balances future ambitions with rapid impact.  You'll work independently to automate manual processes, design and build agents and required data solutions using internal platforms, and enable Finance teams to maintain these solutions long-term. 
You’ll build with your partner teams, not simply deliver solutions to them. You’ll help colleagues move from a manual workflow, to a first AI-enabled win, to a reliable solution they can confidently operate and improve themselves. Success means the workflow stays transformed after the initial build, the team trusts the output, and the people closest to the process can own what comes next. 
You’ll favor learning through building. When possible, you’ll put a useful prototype in front of a Finance user, test it against a real deliverable, and improve it quickly rather than spend weeks describing a theoretical future state. When you encounter platform limitations—which you will—you’ll find creative, supportable approaches, collaborate with Engineering to scope and test custom tools, and escalate strategically when needed.
This role requires a blend of process automation, data operations, technical problem-solving, and stakeholder enablement. You'll spend your time building agents, optimizing data pipelines that feed them, creating knowledge layers that make them more accurate, and training Finance teams to use and maintain them. Success means Finance teams can independently run agents you've built while you provide light support and focus on the next automation opportunity.
Responsibilities
Embed with Finance teams to diagnose workflows, identify high-leverage opportunities, and translate business, data, and control requirements into practical AI and automation solutions.
Build and operationalize AI agents for Finance use cases, delivering end-to-end solutions from prototype through validation, monitoring, documentation, and handoff.
Write and optimize SQL for data extraction, transformation, calculation, and validation, ensuring Finance-facing outputs are accurate, explainable, and reliable.
Design reusable knowledge layers, evaluation methods, validation patterns, data-quality frameworks, and components that improve agent accuracy and accelerate future use cases.
Identify agentic limitations and new possibilities; determine when to use existing capabilities, develop an alternative approach, or partner with Engineering to scope and test custom tools and integrations, including tools using Model Context Protocol where appropriate.
Build alongside users, gather feedback through real deliverables, and iterate until the solution fits the workflow and earns user trust.
Enable long-term ownership through clear SOPs, runbooks, training, and self-service tooling; coach Finance teams to operate, maintain, and evolve what has been built.
Establish monitoring and observability for deployed agents, including metrics, alerting, and incident-response processes that support reliable operation.
Diagnose technical and data issues, resolve problems independently where possible, and collaborate with Engineering when solutions require deeper platform changes.
Measure adoption and impact, share lessons and wins, and turn successful implementations into standards, components, and playbooks for the broader Finance AI portfolio.
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
5+ years of experience in data analytics, technical operations, business intelligence, automation, solutions delivery, or a related field.
Of which, 2+ years of experience in program management, working directly alongside business leaders to develop and execute process transformation programs
Hands-on experience building AI-enabled tools, agents, automations, or workflows that changed a real business process—not solely using AI as a conversational tool, 
Strong SQL proficiency, including experience writing complex queries using CTEs, window functions, and joins for data analysis, transformation, or pipeline logic.
A track record of independently scoping and delivering technical solutions for process improvement, demonstrating ownership from problem definition through adoption.
Strong analytical and investigative skills, including the ability to identify root causes, debug complex data problems, and resolve inconsistencies.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and work effectively with domain experts and Engineering partners.
Experience teaching, coaching, enabling users, or transferring ownership of a solution through documentation, training, or self-service tools.
Working knowledge of development practices such as version control, testing, code review, and iterative delivery.
Experience using low-code tools, scripting, workflow automation, AI-assisted development, or custom integrations, paired with curiosity and the ability to learn evolving technologies.
You will also likely have (not required):
Domain experience in Finance Operations, Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A), Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Payments, or other areas.
Familiarity with modern data tools and practices, such as Python, Databricks, ETL/ELT processes, data pipelines, and data-quality controls.
Experience with Model Context Protocol or another extensibility or integration framework.
Experience navigating financial systems and understanding how data flows through accounting, reporting, reconciliation, forecasting, or payments processes.
Experience with change management, organizational transformation, or large-scale enablement programs.
Experience building internal tools, templates, components, or playbooks that were adopted beyond the original team or use case.
Experience working in a high-growth technology company with rapidly evolving processes and tools.
Note on technical depth: This role involves working at the intersection of no-code AI tools and custom development. While software engineering expertise is not required, you should be comfortable applying technical concepts, collaborating closely with Engineering teams, and using AI-assisted development tools to extend platform capabilities when needed.

Stripe is looking for a senior operator and systems thinker to join the Central Strategy and Operations (S&O) team. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who is obsessed with how organizations actually work and who builds the infrastructure that makes Stripe faster, clearer, and more coordinated as it scales.
Central S&O sits at the center of how Stripe runs as a company. This role specifically owns the machinery of company operations—the planning processes, operating rhythms, information architecture, and cross-functional systems that let the leadership team at Stripe make better decisions, faster. If you're the kind of person who looks at a broken process and immediately starts designing the system that replaces it—and who reaches for automation before asking for headcount—this role is for you.
You'll work across the most senior leaders at Stripe and partner teams to design, run, and continuously improve the operational systems that connect strategy to execution. We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

10+ years of work experience, with a significant portion in operational roles at high-growth tech companies—product operations, strategy and operations, business operations, or company or corporate planning
A track record of building and owning operational systems. You have measurably improved how a company or large team operates, not just managed existing processes.
Deep experience either with company or functional planning—annual planning, OKR and SOKR-style goal-setting, resource allocation, and operating cadence design
A systems thinker who is automation-first—you instinctively reach for tools, data pipelines, and AI-augmented workflows to reduce manual overhead and increase leverage

title: Data Analyst, Intern
location: New York, Seattle, South San Francisco HQ
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible.
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
About the team
Data Science at Stripe is a vibrant community where data analysts and data scientists learn and grow together. You'll work with some of the most fundamental data at Stripe, and use that data to help drive company-wide initiatives. We have a variety of Data Analytics roles and teams across Stripe and will seek to align you to the most relevant team based on your background.
What you’ll do
As an intern at Stripe you’ll work on projects across our stack that directly impact the way millions of businesses operate. You’ll own problems end to end with the support of your manager and teammates. It’s an opportunity to work alongside some of the most creative and technically rigorous data analysts and scientists in the industry. You'll partner deeply with teams across Stripe to ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly. You'll work closely with partners to extract insights from the rich and complex data at Stripe. You'll build metrics, scalable data pipelines, dashboards, and reports to inform and run the business. You'll deliver actionable business recommendations through analyses and data storytelling.
Our internship program is competitive and the expectations are high.
Responsibilities
Analyze data and running experiments to drive impact
Ensure that our users, our products, and our business have the models, data products, and insights needed to make decisions and grow responsibly
Create metrics, reports, and dashboards to inform and run the business
Extend Stripe’s metrics semantic layer
Build new data assets and improve existing data assets to support decision-making, products, and business processes
Assess the impact of decisions, product launches, and product improvements using business analytics and A/B testing
Learn quickly by asking great questions, finding how to work with your mentor and teammates effectively, and communicating the status of your work clearly
Present your work to the Data Science team, partner teams, and fellow interns
Who you are
Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before.
Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
Enrolled in a quantitative Bachelor’s or Master's degree program (e.g. Data Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Mathematics, etc.) with the expectation of graduating in December 2027 or spring/summer 2028
Experience with SQL
Proficiency with AI tools to accelerate model development, analysis, and coding
Experience communicating and collaborating with multidisciplinary stakeholders in a team environment
Preferred qualifications
Experience writing and debugging data pipelines
Demonstrated ability to evaluate and receive feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders via experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects
Ability to learn new systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts

title: Financial Data Analyst Intern, Technical Operations
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a technology company focused on improving the conditions for economic growth and prosperity. We build programmable financial infrastructure, rethinking from first principles how financial services should work, to make it easier and cheaper for any business to start and scale. More than 10 million businesses build on Stripe, spanning the economic frontier—from solo founders to established enterprises—united by a practical focus on growth. The most ambitious companies in the world use Stripe as core infrastructure to grow faster. They process trillions of dollars a year on Stripe, equivalent to around 1.6% of global GDP. While economic growth makes everyone better off, open markets also enable greater variety. When any business can easily serve a global customer base, the quality and diversity of products in the world increase, and craft and creativity are unleashed into the smallest niches. Our own growth is wholly contingent on the success of the businesses building on Stripe. We therefore invest back into our technology at an unusual rate. We make upgrades to our products every single day to deliver compounding gains to our customers. We maintain some of the most reliable APIs on the internet. We build entirely new pieces of financial infrastructure to enable new ideas. And our significant advances in risk and fraud infrastructure over many years are making the internet economy safer and more accessible. 
Though people at Stripe don’t tend to take themselves seriously, Stripe is a fairly serious place: our customers are depending on us for their livelihoods. We admire ambition, intensity, curiosity, humility, and rigor. The most effective people become knowledgeable about many domains besides their own. Any company is an applied exercise in understanding some aspect of society or the market. In working with so many (especially the new and innovative ones), we think that Stripe is one of the very best places to learn about how the world works.
About the team
The APAC Payments TechOps team ensures the accuracy of financial data flowing through Stripe's payment infrastructure, manages aging balances, maintains compliance with partner and regulatory requirements, and builds tooling to detect and resolve data quality issues at scale. Through the internship, you will work with real financial data, gain experience in payments data analysis and operational problem-solving, and have opportunities to present your work to your team and the wider org. Each intern has a dedicated intern manager, and every project is part of the team's roadmap and will directly help Stripe's mission.
What you’ll do
Every internship at Stripe centers around a real, legitimate project that our team urgently needs. We will support you in shipping it. Yes, you will actually ship it. Example projects include building data quality checks for payment flows, creating dashboards to surface aging balance trends, automating compliance reporting, or analyzing cost structures across partner networks. As a Stripe intern, you'll be tackling important projects while working alongside exceptional people who insist on doing their best work. You'll learn from people with high standards who are great at inspiring others to do more and go further. We value technical and personal growth, and see our internship program as a vehicle to foster both.
Responsibilities
Analyze financial data by writing queries and examining data quality, reconciliation accuracy, or cost structures across Stripe's payment flows
Write code or build tooling that will be used in production and has meaningful impact to Stripe's payment operations
Give and receive technical feedback through code reviews, data model discussions, or analysis walkthroughs
Collaborate with engineers, product managers, and finance stakeholders to seek and incorporate feedback on your work
Learn quickly by asking great questions, by working with your intern manager and teammates effectively, and by communicating the status of your work clearly
Who you are
Ambitious builder: You’re energized by building solutions without clear precedent and solving problems with far-reaching consequences. Successful Stripes are deeply curious, and prefer the joy of discovery to the comfort of certainty.
Rigorous thinker: You appreciate that things worth doing are rarely simple. You enjoy working on problems that have never been tackled before. 
Adaptable problem solver: You adapt quickly and treat obstacles as opportunities. At Stripe we embrace kindness while encouraging Stripes to take measured risks and act boldly, even in the absence of consensus.
Minimum requirements
A strong fundamental understanding of quantitative analysis through pursuit of a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in computer science, data science, finance, economics, information systems, or a related discipline
Some experience and familiarity with programming or data analysis, either through side projects or coursework. We work mostly in SQL, Python, and Ruby. We believe new programming languages can be learned if the fundamentals and general knowledge are present
Experience from previous internships or other multi-person projects, including open source contributions, that demonstrate evaluating and receiving feedback from mentors, peers, and stakeholders
Ability to learn unfamiliar systems and form an understanding of those systems, through independent research and working with a mentor and subject matter experts
Preferred qualifications
At least 2 years of university education, or equivalent work experience
Familiarity with SQL and querying relational databases, either through coursework or personal projects
Interest in payments, fintech, or financial systems
Comfort with developer tools (e.g. git) and data visualization
A strong interest in understanding how financial data flows through complex payment systems and ensuring its accuracy
Ability to write clearly to explain analytical findings to stakeholders, team members, and other Stripes

title: Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, Marketing
location: Seattle, San Francisco, New York, Chicago, Atlanta, Remote in the US, Canada
description:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies — from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups — use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. We're building a team of Forward Deployed AI Accelerators (FDAs) embedded directly with marketing cohorts to make AI the default mode for all work — not an occasional tool, but the foundation of how every marketer at Stripe executes.
Today, marketers are already achieving remarkable results — building their own data dashboards, creating agents that compress multi-day processes, and authoring tools that accelerate workflows. The FDA team exists to take what's working and systematically scale it across the entire marketing organization.
What you'll do
As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. You'll build alongside them, and you'll help them fundamentally change how they operate. Your measure of success is the number of workflows you've permanently transformed and the extent to which those in your cohort start any task with an AI tool.
Responsibilities
Identify and document the highest-leverage workflow transformations within your cohort's day-to-day work by deeply understanding their processes and outputs
Build custom tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to each marketer's specific responsibilities
Coach and partner with each marketer through a progressive journey — from awareness, to first win, to regular AI integration, to full workflow transformation, to self-sufficiency
Teach marketers to build and iterate on their own tools over time, creating independence
Recognize patterns across your cohort and systematically scale what works — a tool built for one marketer will be reusable for their peers
Document every tool, playbook, and transformation pattern you build so the entire FDA team uses each other's work
Share wins visibly within your cohort and with leadership to build momentum, inspire, and celebrate success
Track individual and cohort progress rigorously against a defined maturity model, moving every marketer toward self-sustaining, AI-first work
Prepare marketers for an agentic future — not just prompt writing, but designing, building, and overseeing autonomous, multi-agent workflows
Who you are
We're looking for people who have already lived the transformation they'll be driving for others. You've used AI to fundamentally change how work gets done, not as a novelty, but as your default operating mode.
You are a deep AI practitioner. You build agents, automations, and tools fluently. You don't just know what AI can do in theory. You've built things that changed how real teams operate, and the people you built for actually use what you shipped. You build in real time alongside the people you support.
You spot transformation opportunities and execute on them. You look at a team's workflows and see where AI changes the economics: where existing work can be done in a fraction of the time, or where entirely new programs become viable that weren't worth doing before. Then you build the thing, not just the slide.
You understand marketing work. You either have direct experience in marketing or quickly learn the workflows, deliverables, tools, and pressures of your assigned cohort. You know that understanding someone's work is a prerequisite to transforming it.
You are a pattern recognizer. When you build something that works for one person, you immediately see how it applies to others. You think in systems, not one-off solutions.
You are a strong communicator. You explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences, adapt your style to different people, and make progress visible to leadership and stakeholders.
You are high-caliber, persistent, and versatile. Your skills and experience are valuable across the company. You're the kind of person who succeeds in many roles at Stripe.
You bias toward action and speed. You'd rather show someone a working proof-of-concept on their own deliverable today than present a polished deck about what's theoretically possible next quarter.
You are comfortable with ambiguity and evolution. This is a new team building a new operating model. The playbook will be rewritten as we learn. You thrive in that environment.
Minimum requirements
3+ years of professional experience in a role requiring diagnostic thinking, problem-solving, and cross-functional collaboration
Demonstrated, hands-on experience building and deploying AI-powered agents, tools, automations, or workflows that real people use in their actual work, whether that made existing processes meaningfully more efficient or made previously unviable work possible for the first time
Proficiency with AI development tools and platforms (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, custom agent frameworks, API integrations, workflow automation tools)
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and adapt your style to different learners
Comfort working across multiple workstreams and relationships simultaneously (you'll be supporting 25–45 marketers at varying stages of their AI journey)
Track record of coaching, teaching, or enabling others, with evidence that people you've helped actually changed how they work
Preferred qualifications
Experience in a formal AI transformation role where the job was substantially about identifying opportunities for workflow transformation and executing on them with hands-on builds
Experience helping people become more expert AI users and capable builders
Experience in marketing, marketing operations, growth, or a closely adjacent function, including familiarity with marketing technology stacks (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce, analytics platforms, content management tools)

title: Growth Marketing Manager, Greater China
description:
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. About the team
Growth Marketing is a team of performance-driven marketers and channel specialists. We partner closely with growth, creative, analytics and regional marketing to drive revenue through self-serve and sales motions. We work globally, across all Stripe offerings and with all company segments — from startups to the largest enterprises.
What you'll do
As a China Growth Marketer, you will own launching, proving out, and scaling paid media and growth marketing channels for the Chinese market. This is a 0-to-1 role: you'll identify the right channels, build the playbooks, and demonstrate what works before scaling investment. You'll work across paid channels native to China (WeChat, Baidu, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Zhihu, Bilibili, and others), as well as broader growth marketing levers like web optimization, content distribution, and landing page localization for Chinese users.
You will be the in-house expert on how to reach Chinese developers, founders, and business operators through digital channels, bringing deep knowledge of the local ecosystem, platform mechanics, regulatory environment, and user behavior. You'll partner cross-functionally with regional marketing, analytics, creative, product marketing, and sales to ensure paid media supports Stripe's growth objectives in China. 
Responsibilities
Launch and scale paid media channels specific to the China market — including WeChat Ads, Baidu SEM, Douyin/Ocean Engine, Xiaohongshu, Zhihu, Bilibili, and programmatic platforms (e.g., Tencent Guangdiantong, ByteDance Pangolin)
Develop and execute a testing roadmap to prove channel viability: define hypotheses, run experiments, measure incrementality, and make go/no-go recommendations on scaling investment
Own web optimization and landing page localization for Chinese audiences — ensuring Stripe's web presence converts effectively for local users
Build measurement frameworks for China-specific channels, partnering with analytics to attribute performance through to signups, activations, and revenue
Manage campaign budgets, pacing, and performance reporting — communicating results clearly to stakeholders across time zones
Bring the skills and experience to unblock, set up and navigate media platforms and partnerships in the market.
Stay current on China's digital marketing landscape: platform algorithm changes, content regulations, privacy laws (PIPL), and emerging channels
Partner with regional marketing, sales, and product marketing to align paid media with broader China go-to-market strategy
Write concise performance updates and strategic recommendations for a global audience that ranges from paid media specialists to senior leadership
Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum requirements
5+ years of digital marketing experience with significant hands-on experience running paid campaigns on China-native platforms (WeChat, Baidu, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, or similar)
High professional fluency in Mandarin Chinese and English — able to write ad copy, review creative, and communicate strategy in both languages as this role will be heavily involved in the businesses in the Greater China region
Deep knowledge of the China digital marketing ecosystem: platform mechanics, ad formats, targeting capabilities, content regulations, and user behavior patterns
Experience launching new channels from scratch — demonstrated ability to take a channel from 0 to 1, prove its value, and scale it
Strong analytical skills — ability to analyze campaign data, identify trends, and make data-driven optimization decisions
Experience in B2B marketing, SaaS, developer tools, fintech, or high-growth technology companies
Self-starter mentality — ability to drive strategic and tactical work forward with minimal oversight in a fast-moving environment
Excellent written communication skills — can write concise, clear updates for a global audience with varying levels of paid media expertise
Preferred qualifications
7+ years of digital marketing experience with deep China market specialization
Experience marketing to developers or technical audiences in China
Familiarity with China-specific analytics and attribution tools
Experience with web optimization, CRO, or landing page testing for Chinese audiences
Understanding of China's regulatory environment as it relates to digital advertising (PIPL, CAC content regulations, industry-specific ad restrictions)
Experience working in a global company with cross-timezone collaboration

title: GTM Product Marketing Manager, Commerce Experiences
description:
Who we are 
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About the team
The GTM Product Marketing team sits within Stripe's Product Marketing org. We make sure Stripe sellers walk into every conversation prepared, confident, and armed with the right story. As Stripe's center of excellence for general product enablement, we set the standard for how sellers learn and pitch our products, drive consistency across product suites, and act as Marketing's Voice of the Field — surfacing seller insights to sharpen upstream messaging and positioning. We translate product value into seller-ready narratives, resources, and enablement — and we measure our impact on seller confidence and how effectively our teams pitch, qualify, and close.
Stripe's Commerce Experiences products (Optimized Checkout Suite, Link, Terminal, Agentic Commerce) help businesses convert more customers across every channel — from online checkout, to digital wallets, to in-person commerce, to the emerging world of AI-driven shopping. We're looking for an exceptional GTM product marketer to bring Stripe's story to market. In this role, you'll be the connective tissue between product, marketing, and the field. You'll translate complex commerce and checkout capabilities into compelling narratives and seller resources that resonate with our users and drive adoption. You'll equip customer-facing teams to confidently pitch all our solutions, answer technical questions, and speak to the roadmap. You'll also elevate seller and field insights to refine product positioning and messaging.
What you’ll do
As the GTM PMM for Commerce Experiences, you’ll need to quickly build a deep understanding of Stripe’s Commerce Experiences products, buyer personas, and differentiation. You will:
Own the content development and GTM enablement strategy across the sold funnel — creating seller-ready resources (pitch decks, FAQs, value props, talking points) that translate product positioning into clear, differentiated customer value propositions for enterprise, mid-market, and platform buyers.
Partner with Market Intelligence to monitor and understand commerce, checkout, and emerging agentic commerce market trends, competitive dynamics, and seller-facing competitive narratives — synthesize insights, and leverage these to build differentiated positioning.
Design and deliver training programs that build seller expertise across the Commerce Experiences portfolio.
Prepare sellers for major product launch events like Stripe Sessions, and to understand the details of the roadmap product is building.
Leverage data and insights to identify enablement and knowledge gaps, prioritize asset development, launch new content, and measure effectiveness on seller confidence and other KPIs.
Surface field insights on a regular cadence — through monthly readouts and structured retros — to inform core PMM positioning and product roadmap.
Minimum requirements
3+ years of product marketing experience, preferably in B2B tech.
Direct experience with checkout, ecommerce, digital wallets, agentic commerce or other commerce platforms is strongly preferred. 
Experience with Enterprise sales cycles and technical products.
Excellent communication and presentation abilities, with a proven track record of distilling complex strategies into clear, compelling narratives.
Strong stakeholder management skills.
Ability to move quickly without compromising attention to detail or polish.
A self-starter who thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and can manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Comfort with data-driven decision making and measuring marketing impact.
Ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders across Product, Sales, and Marketing, and contribute to alignment on shared goals.
Preferred qualifications
Demonstrated comfort working with, and presenting to, senior leaders across a variety of disciplines.
Strong collaboration skills, a tendency to seek and share alternative views, and an ability to earn stakeholder confidence 
Experience using or building AI-powered tooling to accelerate seller productivity or content development.

The flagship product—an AI-driven, non-invasive cardiac test supported by the ACC/AHA Chest Pain Guidelines called the Heartflow FFRCT Analysis—provides a color-coded, 3D model of a patient’s coronary arteries indicating the impact blockages have on blood flow to the heart. Heartflow is the first AI-driven non-invasive integrated heart care solution across the CCTA pathway that helps clinicians identify stenoses in the coronary arteries (RoadMap™Analysis), assess coronary blood flow (FFRCT Analysis), and characterize and quantify coronary atherosclerosis (Plaque Analysis). Our pipeline of products is growing and so is our team; join us in helping to revolutionize precision heartcare.
Heartflow is a publicly traded company (HTFL) that has received international recognition for exceptional strides in healthcare innovation, is supported by medical societies around the world, cleared for use in the US, UK, Europe, Japan and Canada, and has been used for more than 750,000 patients worldwide.  
This is a product management role for a recent MBA graduate who wants to build products that change how heart disease is diagnosed and managed. You will own a customer-facing area of the Heartflow platform: how it fits into the workflows, systems, and business of the hospitals, imaging centers, and physicians who rely on it. You will combine customer insight, business judgment, and technical curiosity to decide what we build and why, working alongside experienced product leaders who will invest in your growth. Success is measured by products our customers adopt, rely on, and recommend.
WHAT YOU WILL OWN
Customer discovery: Spend time on site with cardiologists, radiologists, CT technologists, and health-system administrators to understand how CCTA programs run end to end, from referral and scan acquisition to interpretation, reporting, and follow-up. Turn what you observe into clear problem statements.
Workflow and integration: Define how the Heartflow platform fits into customers’ clinical and IT environments, including EMR, PACS, and reporting systems. Work with engineering to deliver integrations that reduce friction for sites and clinicians.
Requirements and design: Write user needs, use cases, and functional requirements for your product area. Partner with UX and Product Design on workflows and wireframes, and lead design reviews through to verifiable, shippable features.
Business case and prioritization: Build the business case for features and product extensions, covering market size, customer value, adoption, reimbursement considerations, and revenue impact. Use it to prioritize the roadmap with product leadership and stakeholders.
Delivery: Work with engineering through implementation, make scope and timing trade-offs, evaluate prototypes and builds, and prioritize defects by their impact on customers and patients.
Launch and adoption: Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Professional Education on launch readiness, positioning inputs, training, and onboarding. Track adoption and usage after release and feed what you learn back into the roadmap.
Quality and compliance: Work with Quality and Regulatory to keep requirements traceable and design history audit-ready under design controls. Evaluate every change for its effect on user error, patient safety, privacy, and security.
Communication: Give product leadership and cross-functional partners clear, data-backed updates on progress, customer feedback, and risk.
WHAT YOU BRING
Business judgment: Ability to frame ambiguous problems, size opportunities, build a business case, and defend a recommendation with data and explicit reasoning.
Customer orientation: Real curiosity about how clinicians and hospital teams work, and a habit of grounding decisions in what you observe rather than only what people say.
Technical aptitude: Comfort discussing system design, data flows, and cloud software with engineers, and a willingness to learn healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7, FHIR, and DICOM.
Healthcare interest: Genuine interest in healthcare, medical devices, or digital health. Familiarity with cardiology, medical imaging, or reimbursement is a plus.
Communication: Clear, concise writing and speaking for clinical, technical, and executive audiences.
Influence and collaboration: Ability to align cross-functional teams around a shared goal without formal authority.
Design and usability: A strong eye for workflow and usability, especially where product output informs clinical decisions.
Ownership and adaptability: A bias for action and comfort working where priorities and constraints change, within a regulated environment.
EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE
MBA, recently completed or to be completed before the start date.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences, or a related technical or scientific field strongly preferred.
5–7 years of professional experience before or during your MBA, for example in product management, engineering, consulting, healthcare, medical devices, or health technology.
A product management internship, or experience with FDA-regulated software or Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), is a plus.
Willingness to travel to customer sites (approximately 20%).
This role is on site in our San Francisco, CA or Rohnert Park, CA office.
A reasonable estimate of the base salary compensation range is $160,000 to $175,000, bonus, and equity
